name: Rufous-crowned Elaenia
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to the guianas, southern venezuela, and northern amazonian brazil
description: Nondescript flycatcher restricted to savanna scrub on weathered sandy soils. Told from other elaenias by blurry streaking on underparts, relatively indistinct wingbars, and lack of a crest; rufous in crown is difficult to see in the field.

name: Cuban Bullfinch
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: Endemic to Cuba. A small flocking species of brushy and wooded habitats.

name: Pale Mountain-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Bougainville to guadalcanal and malaita (solomon islands)
description: A long-tailed pigeon with striking plumage contrast. Dark gray on the back and wings with an entirely white underside and tail.

name: Philippine Nightjar
rangeDescription: Philippines (except palawan)
description: A medium-sized night bird of forest and open areas from the lowlands to the mountains. Heavily patterned in various shades of brown, with finely barred underparts, blotching on the chest, and dark wings with large pinkish and white spots and a broad pale bar bordered with black.

name: Cinereous Owl
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern mexico (durango) to veracruz and oaxaca
description: Large, dark-eyed owl restricted to pine and pine-oak forests in western and central Mexico. Apparently rare and local; only known from a handful of sites.

name: Trindade Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds trindade and martim vaz islands (south atlantic ocean)
description: A medium-sized gadfly petrel with long, pointed wings, long tail, and elastic, powerful flight. Bill is short and thick.

name: Black Antbird
rangeDescription: Southern colombia east of andes to northwestern bolivia and southwestern amazonian brazil
description: Long-tailed antbird of lowland rainforest. Most common around tree fall gaps in mature rainforest, and other areas of dense undergrowth.

name: Parrot Crossbill
rangeDescription: Coniferous forest of northeastern europe to western siberia
description: Bull-necked, big-headed crossbill with a deep and heavy bill, otherwise identical to Red Crossbill. Males are red; females and juveniles greenish.

name: Southern Fulmar
rangeDescription: Antarctic circumpolar; ranges widely southern oceans
description: Distinctive, medium-sized silvery-gray petrel. Breeds around Antarctica, but regular migrant north to Chile, especially in winter.

name: Salvadori's Antwren
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southeastern bahia to far northeastern santa catarina)
description: Rare short-tailed antwren found in the understory of humid forests where it is very active and is normally associated with mixed-species flocks. Males are gray with a black throat and dark wing coverts with white spots.

name: Akikiki
rangeDescription: Montane ohia forest of kauai
description: A small, very rare Hawaiian honeycreeper of remote native forests on Kauai. Declining rapidly; found only above 4,000 feet elevation in the eastern ‘Alaka’i Plateau.

name: Plumbeous Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru (cusco) to western bolivia and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher of Andean slopes; rare in southern Peru, more common in Bolivia and northern Argentina. Male is separated from White-winged Black-Tyrant by grayer, less glossy plumage and from Cinereous Tyrant by darker belly.

name: Spot-breasted Antvireo
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (eastern minas gerais to paraná) and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Big-headed chunky antbird with a heavy and slightly hooked bill and shortish tail. Found in the lower and middle levels of forests and forest edges.

name: Black-crested Tit-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of far southern ecuador and western peru (southward to pasco)
description: Beautiful little flycatcher with a spiky crest found in the Andes of northern Peru, just barely reaching over the border into southern Ecuador. Male is quite distinctive with a solid black face, black-and-white streaking, and a long crest that sticks up in front of its white crown.

name: Iranian Ground-Jay
rangeDescription: Desert steppes of central and eastern iran
description: Strange brownish corvid restricted to eastern Iran. Pinkish-buff overall, with a slightly decurved bill and black-and-white wing coverts.

name: Tepui Swift
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela, adjacent northwestern guyana, and northern brazil (roraima)
description: Large, dark swift of tepui highlands. Note generally dark appearance, broad wings, and forked tail.

name: Imperial Snipe
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of colombia to eastern peru
description: Hulking snipe of high-elevation elfin forest in the Andes. Large with a thick, drooping bill.

name: Cyprus Warbler
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of cyprus; winters to near east and northeastern egypt
description: Small, long-tailed Curruca warbler. Upperparts dark with well-patterned wing feathers.

name: Brown Teal
rangeDescription: Great barrier island (off northeastern north island) and other satellite islands (new zealand)
description: Largest of the three endemic New Zealand teal species. Both sexes are primarily dark brown in color.

name: Black-chinned Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Breeds drier parts of southern british columbia to northwestern mexico; winters to southern mexico
description: Small hummingbird found in a variety of woodland and brushy habitats. Male distinctive with purple-and-black throat.
